subject: Next steps & competitive probe plan — DataSift discovery call
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@datasift.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-30T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps & competitive probe plan — DataSift discovery call

Samira — thanks again for taking time today. High-level recap of what we heard and a proposed next-step plan so everyone has alignment. Short version up top, details below.

TL;DR: DataSift wants a focused competitive probe comparing Redwood inference against the hyperscaler baseline for your top-3 production prompts (chat + QA + structured extraction). You asked for concrete tests around hallucination rates, regression checks, latency tail, and per-token cost. We can run the probes in a sandbox you control or in our hosted sandbox (redwood-controlled data) — you said sandbox on your side is preferred if procurement agrees.

Primary concerns you raised:
- Hallucination on long-context QA (especially doc-grounded answers)
- P95/P99 tail latency for 4–8K token sequences
- Cost per 1K tokens at your expected traffic profile (burst + steady)
- Ability to run privately/on-prem because of regulated customer data in EU (you want to validate private deployment roadmap)

Proposed probe matrix (action items):
1) Hallucination/regression suite — run our curated prompts (attached eval-probe-prompts.csv) across:
   - redwood-1.1-q4 (quantized variant)
   - redwood-1.1-std (baseline)
   - hyperscaler-std-32k (your baseline)
   Measure: hallucination rate (false assertions), factuality score, and regression delta vs your golden answers.

2) Latency profile — 10K sample requests at your token distribution (we'll use sample-metrics-template.xlsx) to measure mean, P95, P99 with and without prefix KV caching.

3) Cost simulation — token accounting using your traffic mix, compare batching/streaming config impacts.

4) Security/compliance checklist — we will provide SOC2 artifacts and a short runbook for Private deployment proof-of-concept (if procurement greenlights).

Acceptance criteria (suggested, happy to refine):
- Hallucination rate: Redwood delta <= -15% vs hyperscaler on the QA suite (i.e., fewer hallucinations).
- P95 latency: < 350ms for 512-token median requests in your steady-state profile.
- Token cost: within 20% of hyperscaler after batching/caching gains (we'll show calculations).

Immediate asks from your side:
- Confirm preferred sandbox (your sandbox vs Redwood-hosted).
- Share sample golden answers or a short labeled prompt subset if you want our probes to match your scoring exactly.
- Intro to procurement (we need scope and timelines if you want Private PoC).

I've attached: eval-probe-prompts.csv (the prompt sets we discussed), discovery-notes-20280930.txt (call notes), and a metrics template. Marissa will own running the initial probe and Ben will coordinate infra for the sandbox runs.

Proposed timeline:
- This week (by 10/03): agree on sandbox and accept probe matrix
- Next week (10/04–10/10): run initial hallucin/probe + latency smoke tests
- 10/11: share initial results and adjust probes

If that looks good I'll file a HubSpot task and calendar a 30-min sync for 10/11.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0130
From: Samira Khan <samira@datasift.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataSift Procurement <procurement@datasift.com>
Date: 2028-09-30T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & competitive probe plan — DataSift discovery call

Rishi — really helpful summary, thanks. Quick clarifications:
- We prefer to run probes inside our sandbox for visibility; procurement looped in.
- For acceptance criteria, the hallucination reduction target looks reasonable but can you also provide the absolute metric definition (how you compute hallucination rate) so we can validate?
- Can you send the eval-probe-prompts.csv as a separate downloadable link (we have tight controls on attachments via procurement).

Procurement: what timelines do you need to enable our sandbox? We'll need an MOU for limited access; happy to start that conversation.

Agree to the 10/11 sync — please add a calendar invite and include technical leads from Redwood and our platform team (I'll loop them after procurement confirms).

Best,
Samira

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-09-30T14:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & competitive probe plan — DataSift discovery call

Rishi / Marissa — short ops note from infra side. We can provision a dedicated sandbox namespace for DataSift with the following config:
- Models: redwood-1.1-std, redwood-1.1-q4, hyperscaler-std-32k (we'll proxy the hyperscaler if they provide creds/endpoint).
- KV prefix caching toggle (on/off) for side-by-side runs.
- Load generator script to replay their token distribution (I will use the sample-metrics-template.xlsx).

A couple of asks for Samira/procurement:
- If DataSift wants the hyperscaler endpoint proxied through our infra, we need authorization from their security team (simple IP allowlist + short-term token).
- For hallucin/regression scoring, we need a labeled set (20–50 golden Q/A pairs) to get stable signals. Without labeled data we'll run our default scoring (we'll include exact scoring method).

Acceptance thresholds — propose we publish measurable numbers in the initial report rather than hand-wave. Example (draft):
- Hallucination rate: proportion of responses with unverifiable factual assertions (annotated by labelers)
- Regression: percent of responses degraded vs golden answers (semantic similarity + human check)

I will block 2 engineers for 10/04–10/08 to run the probes; Marissa will own the report.

Ben

Subject: Re: Next steps & competitive probe plan — DataSift discovery call

Samira / procurement — attaching a Drive link to the eval prompts and the probe definitions as requested: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1EvalPromptsCsv (we'll also share a HubSpot secure file if needed).

On the hallucination metric: our pipeline labels candidate assertions and checks against the source documents and knowledge cut (if the answer contains fabrications not supported by the source, it counts as a hallucination). We compute hallucination rate as #responses_with_hallucinated_assertions / #responses in the suite. For regression we compare semantic similarity to golden answers (embedding cosine + hand-check threshold) and report % decrease. We'll include the full scoring doc in the initial report so procurement/security can review it.

Next actions I will take today:
- Create HubSpot deal task DS-2028-07 with the probe matrix and attach the Drive link.
- Send calendar invite for 10/11 10:00am PT (30 mins) for result review.
- Marissa will start baseline runs (redwood-hosted) in parallel so we have comparison numbers if your sandbox takes time to provision.

Thanks — looking forward.

Rishi
